staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The staged patch adds an EOF-based guard before reloading the next DT_HASH chain index in `PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup()`.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced failure is a 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow read while `PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup()` walks an ELF `DT_HASH` chain. The testcase supplies a `DT_HASH` table whose hashed bucket starts at symbol index `3`, but the file contains only one in-bounds chain word, so the next `chains[3]` reload crosses the end of `file_image`.

bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) in PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup (src/p_lx_elf.cpp). While walking ELF DT_HASH chains to resolve symbols the code can index past the end of the chains table and invoke a 32-bit read (via the get32/get_le32 path), causing a 4-byte heap OOB read. A malformed or malicious DT_HASH can therefore trigger crashes and potential information disclosure.
bug_description.normalized: The staged testcase is accepted by `PackLinuxElf32help1()` as an ELF32 `ET_DYN` image and loaded into `file_image`. Its `PT_DYNAMIC` entries point `DT_STRTAB` to file offset `0x30d`, `DT_SYMTAB` to `0x314`, `DT_HASH` to `0x348`, and `DT_STRSZ` to `0x20`. `invert_pt_dynamic()` therefore derives a three-entry dynamic-symbol extent (`symnum_max == 3`) and records `DT_HASH` as the last table before EOF. In `elf_lookup("JNI_OnLoad")` the vulnerable code reads `n_bucket == 164`, hashes the name to bucket `96`, and loads `bucket[96] == 3` as the first symbol index. The existing guards only check that `dynsym[3]` still starts before the next table (`0x344 < 0x348`) and that the first visit counter is not yet circular; `get_dynsym_name(3, ...)` returns `nullptr` because `symnum_max <= 3`, so the loop backedge executes. The missing obligation shown by the patch is a bounds check on the next chain reload: `chains` begins at file offset `0x5e0`, leaving exactly one in-bounds 32-bit chain word before EOF, but vulnerable code evaluates `get_te32(&chains[3])`, i.e. a 4-byte read at file offset `0x5ec`, eight bytes past the file image and four bytes past the 1512-byte heap allocation reported by AddressSanitizer.

source.description: Source. Project code materializes the attacker-controlled ELF bytes into `file_image`; the later `PT_DYNAMIC`, `DT_SYMTAB`, and malformed `DT_HASH` state are all read from this buffer.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 1508-byte ELF32 shared-object image. Within the bytes loaded here, the dynamic segment at file offset `0x1b0` encodes `DT_HASH = 0x348`, `DT_STRTAB = 0x30d`, `DT_SYMTAB = 0x314`, and `DT_STRSZ = 0x20`; at offset `0x348` the `DT_HASH` header stores `n_bucket = 164` and bucket `96 = 3`, while the chains area starts at `0x5e0` and contains only one in-bounds 32-bit word before EOF.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Crash sink. The unchecked `chains[3]` pointer from `PackLinuxElf32::elf_lookup()` reaches this helper through `get_te32()` and `LEPolicy::get32()`, and the inline 4-byte copy performs the AddressSanitizer-reported heap-buffer-overflow read.

root_cause.description: Root cause corresponding to the staged patch. Vulnerable code reloads the next `DT_HASH` chain index from `chains[si]` without first proving that `si` still indexes an in-bounds chain word; the fix adds an EOF-based guard before this backedge read.

tainted_value_origin.description: The malformed dynamic entries and `DT_HASH` words that drive the out-of-bounds chain read all originate from the file bytes loaded into `file_image` here.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific loader gate. The testcase must satisfy the ELF32 magic and program-header-size checks and avoid either explicit endian mismatch branch here, otherwise `PackLinuxElf32help1()` zeroes the header fields and returns before any `PT_DYNAMIC` or `DT_HASH` parsing occurs.

fine_trace.note: Source. The testcase's ELF bytes are copied into `file_image`, including the `PT_DYNAMIC` entries at `0x1b0` and the malformed `DT_HASH` bytes at `0x348`.

The validated `PT_DYNAMIC` program header is converted into an in-memory `dynseg` pointer, so later helper code reads dynamic tags and addresses directly from attacker-controlled bytes in `file_image`.
Dynamic parsing records the sorted starts of the relevant tables. For the testcase the order is `DT_STRTAB = 0x30d`, `DT_SYMTAB = 0x314`, `DT_HASH = 0x348`, then the sentinel `file_size = 0x5e4`.

The dynamic-symbol extent is derived from the distance between `DT_SYMTAB` and the next table start. With `DT_SYMTAB = 0x314` and next offset `0x348`, `tmp2 = 0x34` and `symnum_max = 3`, so symbol indices `0..2` are the only ones considered named entries.
The `DT_HASH` entry is materialized as a pointer into `file_image`. For this testcase `hashtab` resolves to file offset `0x348`.
The vulnerable lookup is reached during shared-object initialization when the code asks `elf_lookup()` to resolve `JNI_OnLoad` using the parsed dynamic tables.

Lookup reconstructs the next-table bounds from `dt_offsets`. Here `l_sym` becomes `file_image + 0x348` because `DT_HASH` follows `DT_SYMTAB`, and `l_hash` becomes `file_image + 0x5e4` because `DT_HASH` is the last table before the EOF sentinel.
The malformed hash header is parsed. The testcase sets `n_bucket = 164`, so `chains` starts at file offset `0x5e0`; because the file ends at `0x5e4`, only `chains[0]` is in bounds.
The lookup target `JNI_OnLoad` hashes to bucket index `96` under the ELF hash algorithm and the testcase's `n_bucket = 164`.
The existing bucket bound check does not reject the testcase. `&buckets[96]` is at file offset `0x4d0`, which is still below `l_hash = file_image + 0x5e4`.
The chosen bucket is read from the malformed table. The testcase stores `bucket[96] = 3`, so the first chain walk starts at symbol index `3`.
The present symbol-table extent check still passes. `dynsym[3]` starts at file offset `0x344`, which is before `l_sym = file_image + 0x348`.
Name resolution does not stop the walk. With `symnum_max = 3` and `symnum = 3`, `get_dynsym_name()` returns `nullptr`, so `elf_lookup()` neither matches `JNI_OnLoad` nor returns a valid symbol.
The circular-chain guard also passes on the first iteration because `n_visit` starts at `0`, so the check only compares `dynsym[0]` at file offset `0x314` against `l_sym = 0x348`.

Root cause. The loop backedge reloads the next chain index without checking whether `si` still fits inside the chains area. Here `si = 3`, but `chains` begins at `0x5e0` and only `chains[0]` is in bounds, so `&chains[3]` is file offset `0x5ec`, eight bytes past EOF and four bytes past the 1512-byte heap allocation reported by AddressSanitizer.
The out-of-bounds `chains[3]` pointer is consumed by the endian helper chain and this inline 4-byte copy performs the crashing heap-buffer-overflow read.

format.name: ELF32 ET_DYN with malformed DT_HASH
format.contract: The testcase must be admitted by `PackLinuxElf32help1()` as an ELF32 shared object whose `PT_DYNAMIC` maps `DT_STRTAB` to `0x30d`, `DT_SYMTAB` to `0x314`, and `DT_HASH` to `0x348`; the `DT_HASH` header must set `n_bucket = 164`, place `bucket[elf_hash("JNI_OnLoad") % 164] = 3`, and leave only one in-bounds 32-bit chain word at file offset `0x5e0`, so the next-loop read of `chains[3]` crosses the end of `file_image`.
